ai.title: Log active handles on close in dev
ai.summary: Added logging of active handles during CLI shutdown when `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` is `dev`. Uses `process._getActiveHandles()` to capture state for debugging. Scoped to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes and closes while running in internal-development mode, it now writes down a list of still-open connections it kept track of during that session. This only happens on development machines used by the team, and you would only know it happened if you were watching the diagnostic logs, where a new line appears recording any remaining handles sitting open at shutdown.

ai.title: Broaden PostHog error suppression in analytics console wrapper
ai.summary: The `wrapConsoleMethod` function in `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` now iterates through all arguments to detect error names, replacing the previous strict check on `args[0]`. This change ensures that PostHog errors are suppressed even when passed as non-first arguments or wrapped in different structures, preventing them from leaking to the user's console.

eli5.text: If you have seen error messages in your browser's console that reference PostHog, those messages are now hidden more reliably than before. Previously, the system only checked the very first piece of information passed to the console to decide whether the message came from PostHog. Now, it scans through every piece of information it receives, so even if the PostHog error is buried among other data or wrapped in a different format, it will still be caught and suppressed. You probably would not notice anything different unless you were actively looking at your browser's console for these specific error messages.

ai.title: Version 1.0.333
ai.summary: Package version incremented to 1.0.333 in `npm-app/package.json`. No functional code changes accompany the bump.

eli5.text: The assistant's version label was updated to a new number, and this release also quietly adds two behind-the-scenes improvements: while the assistant is shutting down during local development, it now logs any lingering background tasks so problems are easier to track down, and a helper that routes errors to the analytics tool now stays quieter so it no longer floods the console with noise. If you look closely, you would see these as quieter, more informative console output during development, with no visible change for regular use.

ai.title: Increase checkpoint file manager buffer limit
ai.summary: The checkpoint file manager in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` now sets `maxBuffer` to 50MB for the git submodule exposure command. Stderr is also changed to 'ignore' to prevent potential buffer overflow or noise from non-critical error streams during large submodule operations.

eli5.text: When the assistant saves a checkpoint that includes linked sub-projects, it now allows up to 50MB of output from that save operation before stopping, and it quietly discards any non-essential warning messages that those sub-projects might print along the way. You won't see this change directly, but if you've ever seen a save fail simply because a large sub-project produced a lot of output, those saves will now succeed instead. The assistant's ability to include sub-projects when saving checkpoints is now more tolerant of large or chatty sub-projects.

ai.title: CLI spinner adds hang detection
ai.summary: CLI `Spinner` tracks `cli.app_hung` event after 60s inactivity. Mechanism uses `setTimeout` in `npm-app/src/utils/spinner.ts` to trigger `trackEvent` with duration. Scope covers `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` enum and CLI spinner utility. Timeout cleared on `stop()` to prevent false positives.

eli5.text: If the assistant stops responding for 60 seconds, the system now quietly records that the assistant appears to have hung so the team can spot and fix stalls. This applies to everyone running the assistant in a terminal right now. You won't see anything different on screen: when the assistant finishes normally the hang tracker just turns off, and it only logs data in the background if a stall is actually detected.

ai.title: Remove release-binaries.yml CI workflow
ai.summary: Deleted .github/workflows/release-binaries.yml, stopping automated binary builds and releases to codebuff-community. This removes the matrix build steps for Linux, macOS, and Windows artifacts. Affects CI pipelines only; no runtime code changes.

eli5.text: The automated system that used to package and publish ready-to-use program files for different operating systems after each major release has been turned off and removed. If you looked at the project's release pages today, you would no longer see the separate download links for those packaged program files that were previously created automatically. This only affects the behind-the-scenes process of creating and sharing those release packages; it does not change how the program itself works or gets installed from its standard source. The project will now rely on its regular installation method for all users.
